summary: Native Node addon harvests browser credentials on require()
details: Package ships a single ~10MB Rust-compiled Node native addon registered as `main`, so its N-API init runs on any consumer `require()`. Extracted strings from the binary include canonical Chromium Login Data harvesting markers (`Found login for`, `TSQLITE_AUTH_USER`, cookie insertion referencing `Cookie.value`), host fingerprinting primitives (`network_adapters`, `/dev/disk/by-id/`, `/etc/lsb-release`, imports of `getifaddrs`/`gethostname`/`execvp`/`posix_spawnp`), and a full embedded HTTP/TLS client stack (`ureq_proto`, TLS 1.3 handshake, `getaddrinfo`/`connect`/`sendmsg`). Despite the presence of a complete networking stack, no plaintext URLs, domains, or IPs appear in the binary — destinations are constructed at runtime, hiding the exfiltration endpoint from static inspection. Package identity reinforces the malicious intent: the name `new-native-tools-linux-x64-gnu` mimics the platform-suffixed native subpackage shape used by @napi-rs/@node-rs, and the version string embeds a unix-timestamp suffix (`...-1785839911`) characteristic of automated typosquat publish campaigns.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
